caption: #anxiety #stress #anxietyisreal
transcript: Sit with this for a moment. Most people believe their anxiety would disappear if they could just know for sure. If only I knew what was going to happen. If only I knew they wouldn't leave. If only I knew I was making the right decision. But the mind plays a strange game. The more certainty you chase, the more anxiety you create. Anxiety is not simply fear. It is a troubled relationship with uncertainty. And once you see this, you cannot unsee it. Look closely at your life. Many people fall into what I call the overs. Overthinking, overworking, overgiving, over explaining, over planning, over communicating. Why? Because the mind believes that if it does more, it can control what happens next. It believes it can prevent rejection, prevent failure, prevent disappointment. But has that ever truly worked? Think about your own experience. The more you overthink, the less peace you feel. The more you try to control every outcome, the more exhausted you become. If overthinking created certainty, one night of worrying would solve the next six months of your life. Yet somehow, the opposite happens. The more you think, the more problems appear. The more you chase certainty, the further peace moves away. Real peace begins when you stop demanding certainty from life. And learn to trust yourself, even when the path ahead is unclear. If this message spoke to you, you'll find more lessons like this in the way back to stillness, linked in my profile.
